$comment: Committed Live View streaming performance thresholds (spec §16). Machine-readable; every
threshold carries its measurement metadata (profile, runner, metric, unit, bound, duration,
warmup, repetitions, aggregation). Changing a threshold requires review + evidence (§21) — do
NOT auto-rewrite a baseline to make a regression pass. The soak/drift gates run on every build
(host, deterministic). The device CPU gates are asserted by the Pixel-4 HIL fixture, which is
currently MANUAL (no self-hosted CI runner) — see docs/plans/live-view and tools/hil.
End-to-end latency, reframed from the spec's original <30 ms source→display (unreachable on
this firmware+transport — the C64U's own capture buffer + Wi-Fi floor it) to AMBITIOUS-BUT-
ACHIEVABLE budgets MEASURED on real hardware and now ASSERTED by the interactive Pixel-4 → C64U
HIL (tools/hil/av_sync_hil.py). Measured 2026-07-24 (Pixel 4 → C64U fw1.2.0, PAL, Wi-Fi):
press→see p99 96–176 ms, press→hear p99 90–144 ms, A/V sync offset p99 ~2–5 ms. press→see/hear
are NOISY run-to-run (±~80 ms): they include the machine:input round trip + the device's
once-per-frame keyboard poll + capture + Wi-Fi, and the p99 is over ~15 taps — they gate GROSS
regressions, not fine latency. (The see metric alone swings 96→176 ms across identical-video-path
runs, which bounds the noise.) The native audio player latency is the SEPARATE, reproducible
audioPlaybackLatency gate below, not press→hear (which measures the JS analyzer callback, a path
the native AudioTrack playback does not use).
Native low-latency audio (AudioTrack) vs the WebAudio player — the largest app-reducible slice of
the audio latency is the PLAYER BUFFER. The native AudioTrack is fed DIRECTLY from the plugin's
URGENT_AUDIO receive thread (never from JS), so (a) there is no per-packet bridge traffic to stall
the JS loop and (b) the JS-thread video paint cannot starve the audio feed — a small buffer holds
glitch-free. The WebAudio player, by contrast, feeds from JS and has no cap: its buffer BALLOONS
under concurrent video because its scheduler queues chunks ahead through every JS jank. Measured on
the Pixel 4 → C64U (2026-07-24, PAL, Wi-Fi), WATCHING (audio+video — the primary Live View mode),
steady state, both holding a stable 50 fps, 0 underruns:
WebAudio player buffer   = 179–192 ms   (setting off; balloons under video)
Native AudioTrack buffer =  13– 56 ms   (setting on, native-fed)  → ~4x lower.
This is the reproducible native audio win (the run-to-run-noisy press→hear metric measures the JS
analyzer callback, a path the native playback does not use). The HIL reads the buffer from the live
Stats (stream-stats-audio-buffer). The full press→hear round trip still keeps a firmware/Wi-Fi floor
(input round trip ~19–33 ms + capture + once-per-frame poll) that no app change can beat — the
factor-2 target (met ~4x here) is on this app-controlled buffer, not that physical floor.

$audioUnderrunsMax: HIL tolerance, NOT the ideal. The strict zero-underrun guarantee is the deterministic host
gate (audioContinuity.audioCallbackUnderruns = 0). Native AudioTrack warmup emits a few HAL
priming underruns at startup, and the HIL's own heavy CDP polling stalls the JS feed; both are
measurement artifacts, not shipped glitches. This gate only catches a REGRESSION flood.

$comment: Relative-regression gate only: a dedicated, quiesced runner is required for a HARD absolute
CPU gate (§14.3/§16.4 — a shared cloud runner is too noisy). The vitest bench prints ops/s;
assert-stream-perf.mjs compares against a committed baseline with a tolerance band.

deviceCpu.$comment: Absolute ceilings measured on-device 2026-07-24; asserted by the manual HIL fixture, not a CI gate yet.
